guide.title: How to Use the Nutrition Calculator

howToUse.title: Usage
items: Find a food by search or category and tap it to add one serving to 'My Meal' (tap again to add another serving)
Enter the amount in g (ml for drinks) or use the 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 / 2 serving buttons
For foods not listed, use 'Enter from a nutrition label' with the values on the package
Nutrition Facts shows calories, sodium, carbs, protein and fat as % of Daily Values; the macro ratio shows whether you are within the recommended ranges
Share, save as image or copy the link. Opening the link restores the same meal

macros.title: Macronutrients and Daily Values
items: Carbohydrate: 4 kcal/g, main energy source. Daily Value 324g; recommended 50–65% of calories
Protein: 4 kcal/g, builds muscle and enzymes. Daily Value 55g; recommended 10–20%
Fat: 9 kcal/g, hormones and cell membranes. Daily Value 54g; recommended 15–30%
Sodium: Daily Value 2,000mg. A bowl of Korean soup, stew or noodles can contain 1,500–4,000mg
Daily Values follow the MFDS food labeling standards (2,000 kcal basis); ranges follow the 2025 Dietary Reference Intakes for Koreans

tips.title: Healthy Eating Tips
items: Distribute daily calories: breakfast 30%, lunch 40%, dinner 30%
Adequate protein helps you feel full longer
Soups and stews can be high in sodium — limit broth intake
Adding vegetables to high-fat foods like pork belly or fried chicken adds fiber, but the calories and fat stay the same — watch the portion
Don't forget drink calories — lattes, soju, and beer add up quickly

whatIs.title: What is the Nutrition Calculator?
whatIs.description: A tool that calculates calories and three macronutrients (carbohydrates, protein, fat) for meals using a Korean food database. Enter your daily meals to see total nutritional intake and how it compares to recommended daily allowances. Use it for diet management, muscle building, or dietary control for conditions like diabetes and hypertension.

items.q: What are the recommended macronutrient ratios?
items.a: The 2025 Dietary Reference Intakes for Koreans set adult ranges of 50–65% carbohydrate, 10–20% protein and 15–30% fat. For muscle gain raise protein; for weight loss adjust total calories, carbs and sugars first.

items.q: What if a food isn't in the database?
items.a: Tap 'Enter from a nutrition label' and enter the serving size (g) plus calories, carbs, protein, fat and sodium from the package. Custom foods are saved in the share link too.

items.q: How many calories do I need per day?
items.a: Estimated energy requirements in the 2025 Korean DRIs are 2,600 kcal (men) / 2,000 kcal (women) at ages 19–29, 2,500 / 1,900 kcal at 30–49 and 2,200 / 1,700 kcal at 50–64. Needs vary with activity, so check yours with the Calorie Calculator.

items.q: What's the difference between calories per 100g and per serving?
items.a: Labels show values per 100g (ml) or per serving. This calculator shows each food's serving weight and calories per 100g, and converts automatically when you enter the amount in grams.
